subject: Post-call: DPA role mapping, PII scope & evidence request
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@healthsync.com>, Alice Park <alice@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DPA role mapping, PII scope & evidence request

Hi Jacob / Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap + action items so we’re all aligned on scope and next steps for the DPA / privacy questions you raised. I’ve kept internal folks cc’d for follow-up.

Call highlights (15 min):
- You confirmed HealthSync will be sending Redwood only pseudonymized patient IDs and associated prompt text for enrichment use cases (no direct identifiers stored by default).
- Main asks from your legal/security team: clarity on controller vs. processor responsibilities in the DPA, subprocessors list, breach notification timeline, and ability to provide redacted logs or evidence on request.
- Residency: you prefer EU data residency for one test environment and US for production; we discussed how Private deployment vs Hosted can address that.

Action items / immediate asks for HealthSync (Jacob/Alice):
1) Can you confirm the exact fields you consider "PII" for this integration (e.g., name, SSN, DOB, contact email)? A short CSV of field names helps us map the DPA roles.
2) Please share a copy of the standard HealthSync DPA redline windows/notice periods (if available) so we can align timelines.

Action items from Redwood (assigned):
- Tessa: send draft DPA addendum with clear controller/processor table and proposed 72-hour initial notification window (attached draft). Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf
- Ben: export current subprocessor registry and indicate encryption-in-transit/at-rest for each (attachment: subprocessor_list_2028-03.csv).
- Rishi / Security: confirm SOC2 evidence items we can share and expected turnaround.

If we can get the PII field list and your legal redline by Monday 3/20, Ben and I will prepare an evidence packet and a proposed DPA redline for your counsel.

Thanks — short and pragmatic is best here, happy to jump on a follow-up with your counsel.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1-415-555-0194
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf (draft, highlights enabled)
From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@healthsync.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice@healthsync.com>, HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA role mapping, PII scope & evidence request

Tessa — thanks for the summary. Confirming a couple of things from our side before we share the PII field list with Legal: 

1) PII scope: we treat name, email, phone, DOB, SSN, and patient_medical_id as identifiers. However, we will send you a pseudonymized patient_medical_id mapped client-side. Does that change Redwood's intended obligations under the DPA?

2) Breach notification: we typically expect a 24–48 hour initial notification for incidents that likely impact PHI; is Redwood comfortable with 48 hours for an initial alert and 7 days for a follow-up with evidence?

3) Subprocessors: can you flag any subprocessors that will see cleartext data vs those that only work on encrypted tokens/KV cache? That will speed our legal review.

We’ll loop Legal once we have the field list — aiming to send it today.

— Jacob
Jacob Lee
Senior PM, Integrations | HealthSync
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@healthsync.com>, Alice Park <alice@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA role mapping, PII scope & evidence request

Jacob — perfect, thanks. Quick answers below, and I’ve attached the current draft addendum for your counsel to review (Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf).

- Pseudonymized identifiers: If HealthSync sends only a pseudonymized patient_medical_id (no direct name/email/SSN/DOB), Redwood would still be a processor for the processing performed on that data. If HealthSync retains the re-identification map, that supports a processor relationship. We call this out explicitly in section 2.1 of the attached addendum.

- Notification windows: We can accept an initial notification within 48 hours and a fuller evidence packet within 7 business days for incidents that meet your PHI-impact threshold. For high-severity incidents (unauthorized exfiltration of clear identifiers), we propose a 24-hour expedited channel — Rishi and Grace are copied to confirm operational feasibility.

- Subprocessors and data visibility: see attachment subprocessor_list_2028-03.csv (we’ve indicated a column "data_visibility" with values: "cleartext", "encrypted-only", "none"). Ben, Grace: can you confirm the visibility column is up-to-date?

Next steps I recommend:
1) HealthSync to share the CSV of PII fields (Jacob) — sample layout below.
2) Legal to redline the attached DPA addendum.
3) Redwood to prepare SOC2 artifact list and an anonymized log sample showing tokenization and KV cache TTLs.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min session next week for legal + security to go through the addendum clause-by-clause.

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_list_2028-03.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@healthsync.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA role mapping, PII scope & evidence request

Jacob / Tessa / team —

Following up with the subprocessor & evidence side. Attached is a current registry export (subprocessor_list_2028-03.csv) and a short SOC2 summary we can share to support your security review (SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf). Quick notes: 

- Encryption: all data in transit is TLS1.3; at-rest uses AES-256. Subprocessors flagged as "cleartext" are limited to a small tokenization microservice running in a restricted VPC; access is logged and gated by RBAC.
- Logs & retention: request-level logs are retained for 90 days in hosted accounts by default; with Dedicated/Private deployments we can support custom retention and region controls.
- Evidence turnaround: for routine legal evidence requests we can assemble and deliver within 7 business days; for high-priority incidents we pull priority and aim for 48–72 hours depending on scope.

Grace — can you add specific SOC2 artifact names we can hand to HealthSync Legal (e.g., control IDs, redacted sample report)?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf

On a side note: happy to set up a joint call with Grace + Rishi next Tue 3/21 10am PT if that works for HealthSync legal.
